Kaingang

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Southern Jê *ra (“sun”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ɔ̃ˈɹ̃ɔ̃]

Noun

[edit]

rã

  1. sun

Portuguese

[edit]
Portuguese Wikipedia has an article on:
rã
Wikipedia pt

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • arrã, raã, rãa (obsolete)
  • ran (pre-standardization spelling)

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese rãa, from Latin rana. Compare Galician ra and Spanish rana.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈʁɐ̃/ [ˈhɐ̃]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈʁɐ̃/ [ˈhɐ̃]
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /ˈʁɐ̃/ [ˈχɐ̃]
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈʁɐ̃/

  • Rhymes: -ɐ̃
  • Hyphenation: rã

Noun

[edit]

rã f (plural rãs, diminutive rãzinha)

  1. true frog, ranid
    Synonym: ranídeo
    Coordinate terms: sapo, perereca
    Eu li que pernas de rã são um prato típico da culinária francesa.
    I've read that frog legs are a typical dish in French cuisine.

Vietnamese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Compare rữa (“to decompose”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Hà Nội) IPA(key): [zaː˦ˀ˥]
  • (Huế) IPA(key): [ʐaː˧˨]
  • (Saigon) IPA(key): [ɹaː˨˩˦]

Verb

[edit]

rã • (吔, 𣳮)

  1. to dissolve, to decay, to decompose

Derived terms

[edit]

  • rã đám
  • rã nát
  • rã rời
  • tan rã
